column1: tension.expansion-boundaries|tension|expansion|boundaries|90|The wish to widen possibilities meets a need to protect capacity. Neither has to cancel the other: a bounded experiment lets openness and a clear limit coexist.|define one small experiment and the limit at which you will stop or review it.|What can remain open while one important limit is protected?

tension.connection-solitude|tension|connection|solitude|85|The cards place shared exchange beside private reflection. Closeness may become more useful when there is room to think separately and a clear way to return.|name a short period for private reflection and a specific point for reconnecting.|What needs to be understood privately before it can be shared honestly?

tension.change-stability|tension|change|stability|85|An impulse to revise meets a need for continuity. Preserve one working support while testing a change elsewhere, so revision does not require abandoning every foundation.|choose one thing to keep steady while changing one small part of the arrangement.|Which support is worth preserving while the form around it changes?

tension.effort-rest|tension|effort|rest|90|Persistence and recovery pull on the same limited capacity. More pressure is not the only form of commitment; bounded effort followed by a real pause can protect both progress and attention.|choose a ten-minute task and a stopping point, then take a pause before deciding whether to continue.|What amount of effort remains useful before attention begins to deteriorate?

tension.clarity-uncertainty|tension|clarity|uncertainty|80|A desire for a clear answer meets incomplete information. Use what can be checked without turning the remaining uncertainty into either certainty or a reason to do nothing.|write one established fact beside one open question and identify a way to check that question.|What can you act on responsibly while leaving an uncertain conclusion open?

tension.care-boundaries|tension|care|boundaries|88|Care needs a sustainable edge. Support becomes more dependable when it is specific, wanted and within capacity, rather than measured by how much the giver can absorb.|offer one specific form of support with an honest limit on its time or scope.|How could a clear limit protect the care you actually want to offer?

complement.clarity-effort|complement|clarity|effort|65|A concern with clarity appears before a concern with effort. This is a possible sequence, not proof that the first issue is resolved: check the distinction before building more work on it.|turn one clarified question into a short practical test with an observable result.|What would this attempt help you learn rather than merely demonstrate?

complement.care-connection|complement|care|connection|65|A concern with care appears before a concern with connection. Check what support is needed and available before proposing an exchange; neither generosity nor reciprocity can be assumed.|make one specific request or offer and ask whether it would actually help.|How can support become a conversation rather than an assumption?

complement.release-change|complement|release|change|65|A concern with release appears before a concern with change. Check whether an old demand can be reduced before adding a new direction; the cards do not establish that an ending has already happened.|set aside one completed or outdated obligation before choosing a replacement task.|What space needs to be cleared so the next change is a choice rather than an added burden?
